title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: GeoThinneR R package designed efficient spatial thinning point data, particularly useful species occurrence data spatial analyses. implements optimized neighbor search algorithms based kd-trees, providing efficient, scalable, user-friendly approach. working large-scale datasets containing hundreds thousands points, applying thinning manually possible, existing tools R providing thinning methods species distribution modeling often lack scalability computational efficiency. Spatial thinning widely used across many disciplines reduce density spatial point data selectively removing points based specified criteria, threshold spacing grid cells. technique applied fields like remote sensing, improves data visualization processing, well geostatistics, spatial ecological modeling. Among , species distribution modeling key area thinning plays crucial role mitigating effects spatial sampling bias. vignette provides step--step guide thinning GeoThinneR using simulated real-world datasets.

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: get started GeoThinneR, begin loading packages used vignette: ’ll use two dataset demonstrate use GeoThinneR: simulated dataset n = 2000 random occurrences randomly distributed within 20 x 10 degree area two artificial species. real-world dataset containing loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) occurrences Mediterranean Sea downloaded GBIF included package. Let’s visualize datasets thinning:
code: library(GeoThinneR) library(terra) library(sf) library(ggplot2) # Set seed for reproducibility set.seed(123)  # Simulated dataset n <- 2000 sim_data <- data.frame(   lon = runif(n, min = -10, max = 10),   lat = runif(n, min = -5, max = 5),   sp = sample(c("sp1", "sp2"), n, replace = TRUE) )  # Load real-world occurrence dataset data("caretta")  # Load Mediterranean Sea polygon medit <- system.file("extdata", "mediterranean_sea.gpkg", package = "GeoThinneR") medit <- sf::st_read(medit)

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: Now data ready, let’s use GeoThinneR spatial thinning. methods accessed thin_points() function, requires, minimum, dataset containing georeferenced points (WGS84 CRS - EPSG:4326) matrix, data.frame, tibble format. query dataset provided data argument, lon_col lat_col parameters, can define column names containing longitude latitude (x, y) coordinates. Default values “lon” “lat”, present, take first two columns default. thinning method defined using method parameter, following options: "distance": Distance-based thinning "grid": Grid-based thinning "precision": Precision-based thinning thinning constraint (distance, grid resolution decimal precision) depends method chosen (detailed next section). Regardless method, algorithm selects points retain remove. Since selection non-deterministic, can run multiple randomized thinning trials maximize number retained points. Let’s quickly thin simulated dataset using simple distance-based method: command applies spatial thinning ensuring two retained points closer 20 km (thin_dist). specified run 5 random trials (trials). default, returns trial retains largest subset points, set all_trials = TRUE, trials returned.
code: # Apply spatial thinning to the simulated data quick_thin <- thin_points(   data = sim_data,     # Dataframe with coordinates   lon_col = "lon",     # Longitude column name   lat_col = "lat",     # Latitude column name   method = "distance", # Method for thinning   thin_dist = 20,      # Thinning distance in km,   trials = 5,          # Number of trials   all_trials = TRUE,   # Return all trials   seed = 123           # Seed for reproducibility )  quick_thin #> GeoThinned object #> Method used: distance  #> Number of trials: 5 (5 trials returned) #> Points retained in largest trial: 1390

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: Distance-based thinning (method="distance") ensures retained points separated least user-defined minimum distance thin_dist (km). geographic coordinates, using distance = "haversine" (default) computes great-circle distances, alternatively, Euclidean distance 3D Cartesian coordinates (depending method) identify neighboring points within distance threshold. algorithm iterates dataset removes points close . general, choice search method depends size dataset desired thinning distance: search_type="brute": Useful small datasets, low scalability. search_type="kd_tree": memory-efficient, better scalability medium-sized datasets. search_type="local_kd_tree" (default): Faster "kd_tree" reduces memory usage. Can parallelized improve speed. search_type="k_estimation": fast number points remove low clustered, similar worse "local_kd_tree". can find benchmarking results method package manuscript (see references).
code: dist_thin <- thin_points(sim_data, method = "distance", thin_dist = 25, trials = 3) plot(dist_thin)

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: common greedy method calculating distance points (search_type="brute"), directly computes pairwise distances retains points far enough apart based thinning distance. default, computes Haversine distance using rdist.earth() function fields package. distance = "euclidean", computes Euclidean distance instead. main advantage method computes full distance matrix points. However, main disadvantage time memory consuming, requires computing pairwise comparisons.
code: brute_thin <- thin_points(   data = sim_data,   method = "distance",   search_type = "brute",   thin_dist = 20,   trials = 10,   all_trials = FALSE,   seed = 123 ) nrow(largest(brute_thin)) #> [1] 1390

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: kd-tree binary tree partitions space regions optimize nearest neighbor searches. search_type="kd_tree" method uses nabor R package implement kd-trees via libnabo library. method memory-efficient brute force. Since implementation kd-trees based Euclidean distance, working geographic coordinates (distance = "haversine"), GeoThinneR transforms coordinates XYZ Cartesian coordinates. Although method scales better brute-force method large datasets, since want identify neighboring points query point, performance can still improved large datasets.
code: kd_tree_thin <- thin_points(   data = sim_data,   method = "distance",   search_type = "kd_tree",   thin_dist = 20,   trials = 10,   all_trials = FALSE,   seed = 123 ) nrow(largest(kd_tree_thin)) #> [1] 1390

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: reduce complexity searching within single huge kd-tree containing points dataset, propose simple modification: creating small local kd-trees dividing spatial domain multiple smaller regions, tree (search_type="local_kd_tree"). notably reduces memory usage, allowing thinning method used large datasets personal computers. Additionally, can run parallel method improve speed using n_cores parameter.
code: local_kd_tree_thin <- thin_points(   data = sim_data,   method = "distance",   search_type = "local_kd_tree",   thin_dist = 20,   trials = 10,   all_trials = FALSE,   seed = 123 ) nrow(largest(local_kd_tree_thin)) #> [1] 1390

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: Another way reduce computational complexity kd-tree neighbor searches limiting number neighbors find. nabor::knn() function, can specify number neighbors search (k). spatial thinning, need identify neighbors point, increases computational cost setting k total number points (n). However, search_type="k_estimation" method, can estimate maximum number neighbors point can based spatial density points, thereby reducing k parameter. method particularly useful datasets highly clustered, estimates smaller k value, significantly reducing computational complexity.
code: k_estimation_thin <- thin_points(   data = sim_data,   method = "distance",   search_type = "k_estimation",   thin_dist = 20,   trials = 10,   all_trials = FALSE,   seed = 123 ) nrow(largest(k_estimation_thin)) #> [1] 1390

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: Grid sampling standard method area divided grid, n points sampled grid cell. method fast memory-efficient. drawback ensure minimum distance points. two main ways apply grid sampling GeoThinneR: () define characteristics grid, (ii) pass grid raster (terra::SpatRaster). first method, can use thin_dist parameter define grid cell size (distance km approximated degrees define grid cell size, one degree roughly 111.32 km), can pass resolution grid (e.g., resolution = 0.25 0.25x0.25-degree cells). want align grid external data covariate layers, can pass origin argument tuple two values (e.g., c(0, 0)). Similarly, can specify coordinate reference system (CRS) grid (crs). Alternatively, can pass terra::SpatRaster object, grid used thinning process.
code: system.time( grid_thin <- thin_points(   data = sim_data,   method = "grid",   resolution = 1,   origin = c(0, 0),   crs = "epsg:4326",   n = 1, # one point per grid cell   trials = 10,   all_trials = FALSE,   seed = 123 )) #>    user  system elapsed  #>   0.019   0.000   0.017 nrow(largest(grid_thin)) #> [1] 200 rast_obj <- terra::rast(xmin = -10, xmax = 10, ymin = -5, ymax = 5, res = 1) system.time( grid_raster_thin <- thin_points(   data = sim_data,   method = "grid",    raster_obj = rast_obj,   trials = 10,   n = 1,   all_trials = FALSE,   seed = 123 )) #>    user  system elapsed  #>   0.006   0.000   0.003 nrow(largest(grid_raster_thin)) #> [1] 200

title: Getting started with GeoThinneR
text: scenarios, may want prioritize certain points based specific variable, coordinate uncertainty, data quality, variable. priority parameter allows assign numeric weight point, higher values indicate higher importance, points likely retained thinning. feature available "distance", "grid" "precision" methods. example, sea turtle data downloaded GBIF, column named coordinateUncertaintyInMeters. prioritize records lower uncertainty, can invert values smaller uncertainties receive higher priority. simple way : apply thinning using priority weights: Notes Higher priority values mean point likely retained. "grid" "precision" methods, multiple points fall grid cell rounded coordinate, one highest priority kept. "distance" method, priority used resolve tie situations multiple points spatial influence; point lowest priority dropped. multiple points priority, one selected random. default, provided NA values priority, treated lowest possible priority.
code: # Invert uncertainty to give more priority to lower uncertainty records priority <- -caretta$coordinateUncertaintyInMeters  # For example, handle NAs by assigning lowest possible priority priority[is.na(priority)] <- min(priority, na.rm = TRUE) - 1 # Standard grid thinning (no priority) grid_thin <- thin_points(   data = caretta,   lon_col = "decimalLongitude",   lat_col = "decimalLatitude",   method = "grid",   resolution = 2,   seed = 123 )  # Grid thinning with priority priority_thin <- thin_points(   data = caretta,   lon_col = "decimalLongitude",   lat_col = "decimalLatitude",   method = "grid",   resolution = 2,   priority = priority,   seed = 123 )  mean(largest(grid_thin)$coordinateUncertaintyInMeters, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 35513.54 mean(largest(priority_thin)$coordinateUncertaintyInMeters, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 138288

title: Efficient Spatial Thinning of Species Occurrences
text: GeoThinneR R package designed efficient spatial thinning species occurrence records geospatial point data. integrates three primary thinning methods (distance-based, grid-based, precision-based thinning) single package, eliminating need switch multiple tools. GeoThinneR implements algorithms based kd-tree structures nearest-neighbor searches, significantly improving performance scalability large datasets. Additionally, package provides custom functionalities useful species distribution modeling (SDM), thinning group (e.g., multiple species), retaining exact number points, prioritizing records based user-defined variables. features make GeoThinneR valuable tool handling large-scale occurrence datasets.  GeoThinneR developed alternative tool spatial thinning mitigate effects sampling bias SDM. Various approaches exist address sampling bias, suited different scenarios. references discussing methods bias correction spatial thinning: Boria, R. ., Olson, L. E., Goodman, S. M., & Anderson, R. title: Perform Distance-Based Thinning — distance_thinning
text: coordinates matrix coordinates thin, two columns representing longitude latitude. thin_dist positive numeric value representing thinning distance kilometers. trials integer specifying number trials run thinning. Default 10. all_trials logical indicating whether return results attempts (`TRUE`) best attempt points retained (`FALSE`). Default `FALSE`. search_type character string indicating neighbor search method `c("local_kd_tree", "k_estimation", "kd_tree", "brute")`. default value `local_kd_tree`. See details. target_points Optional integer specifying number points retain. `NULL` (default), function tries maximize number points retained. priority numeric vector length number points, specifying priority weight point. Higher values indicate higher importance favored selecting points retain. Priority used guide selection multiple candidate points otherwise equally valid (e.g., points grid cell, rounded coordinates, number neighbors). distance Distance metric use `c("haversine", "euclidean")`. title: Perform Distance-Based Thinning — distance_thinning
text: - `"kd_tree"`: Uses single kd-tree efficient nearest-neighbor searches. - `"local_kd_tree"`: Builds multiple smaller kd-trees better scalability. - `"k_estimation"`: Approximates maximum number neighbors per point reduce search complexity. - `"brute"`: Computes pairwise distances (inefficient large datasets).

text: `GeoThinned` object (S3 class), contains: `retained`: list logical vectors (one per trial) indicating retained points. `original_data`: original input dataset. `method`: thinning method used. `params`: list thinning parameters used. default, `thin_points()` returns trial largest number retained points. access thinning trials, set `all_trials = TRUE`; otherwise, functions `largest()` `get_trial()` always refer subset.

title: Spatial Thinning of Points — thin_points
text: following thinning methods available: `"distance"` Forces specific minimum distance points. `"grid"` Applies grid-based thinning method. `"precision"` Utilizes precision-based thinning. Distance-based thinning specific parameters distance-based thinning : `thin_dist` positive numeric value representing thinning distance kilometers. `search_type` character string indicating neighbor search method 'c("local_kd_tree", "k_estimation", "kd_tree", "brute")'. defult value 'local_kd_tree'. `distance` Distance metric use 'c("haversine", "euclidean")'. Default Haversine geographic coordinates. `R` radius Earth kilometers. Default 6371 km. `target_points` Optional integer specifying number points retain. 'NULL' (default), function tries maximize number points retained. `n_cores` Number cores parallel processing ('"local_kd_tree"'). Default 1. Grid-based thinning specific parameters grid-based thinning : `thin_dist` positive numeric value representing thinning distance kilometers. `resolution` numeric value representing resolution (degrees) raster grid. provided, takes priority 'thin_dist'. `origin` numeric vector length 2 (e.g., 'c(0, 0)'), specifying origin raster grid (optional). `raster_obj` optional 'terra::SpatRaster' object use grid thinning. provided, raster object used instead creating new one. `n` positive integer specifying maximum number points retain per grid cell (default: 1). `crs` optional CRS (Coordinate Reference System) project coordinates raster (default WGS84, 'epsg:4326'). can EPSG code, PROJ.4 string, 'terra::crs' object. `priority` numeric vector length number points numerical values indicating priority point. Instead eliminating points randomly, higher values preferred thinning. Precision-based thinning specific parameters precision-based thinning : `precision` positive integer specifying number decimal places coordinates rounded. Default 4. `priority` numeric vector length number points numerical values indicating priority point. Instead eliminating points randomly, higher values preferred thinning. information specific thinning methods inputs, refer respective documentation: `distance_thinning()` `grid_thinning()` `precision_thinning()`

title: GeoThinneR 2.1.0 - 24/11/2025
text: "grid" "precision" methods now handle priority ties randomly selecting among equally prioritized points. Updated vignette section priority parameter. Added s2 (>= 1.1.0) Suggests DESCRIPTION file.

title: GeoThinneR 2.0.0 - 24/04/2025
text: CRAN release: 2025-04-24 Breaking changes. version backward-incompatible earlier versions GeoThinneR.

title: GeoThinneR 2.0.0 - 24/04/2025
text: Introduced new GeoThinned S3 class represent thinning results. calls thin_points() now return GeoThinned object instead list logical vectors data frames. print() summary() inspection. plot() visual comparison thinned vs. original data. largest() retrieve trial retained points. largest_index() get index best trial. get_trial() access specific trials. Redesigned thin_points() return structured output provide consistent user interface. Output structure behavior thinning methods updated compatibility new object-oriented design. improved thinning algorithms implementing two new modifications kd-tree method: local kd-trees (local_kd_tree) restricted search (k_estimation). round hashing method (round_hash) now deprecated removed package presenting lower accuracy distance-based methods. thinning method argument method now includes three main thinning strategies implemented GeoThinneR better understanding usability. : “distance”, “grid”, “precision”. search_type argument included distance-based thinning (method = "distance") select search algorithms (“brute”, “kd_tree”, “local_kd_tree”, “k_estimation”). n argument grid-based thinning (method = "grid") now lets specify number points retain per grid cell.

title: GeoThinneR 2.0.0 - 24/04/2025
text: long_col argument now called lon_col consistency lat_col argument. default column names (lon_col `lat_col’) changed “decimalLongitude” “decimalLatitude” “lon” “lat”. Improved documentation, error messages, reproducibility behavior across functions. Updated package vignette reflect changes.
